items.text: On Linux, Ctrl+Shift+N opens the machine chooser: your machines, what is still running on each, and Resume for a session a Disconnect left.
On Linux, the machine chooser's account row signs in and out with Google, and says when your sign-in is kept in a private file.
On Linux, a remote window names its machine in the title bar, and a dropped link comes back on its own with the same shells.
On Linux, a sign-out that cannot remove this machine offers Sign Out Anyway, and the removal finishes itself.
An unfocused pane's dim now covers its read-only badge, bell frame and hover tint, as on Mac.
On Linux, a close confirmation answered Cancel now actually goes away.
On Linux a quit now frees every window, so a debug build exits 0 instead of aborting.
The all-windows sidebar folds and unfolds as a drag picks an item up and lets it go, instead of jumping.
Background windows' all-windows sidebars stop re-reading every title tick and catch up when activated.
